status: CURRENT ALGEBRA DEMOS/INVESTIGATIONS VISUAL CONTRACT — Demo uses student-recorded evidence instead of repeated carry-forward boxes and ends in discussion; Demo guide has slide replicas + detailed notes; Investigation guide preserves overview and adds answered task + end-synthesis walkthrough; Investigation student surface remains clean.

rules: when a later slide depends on earlier evidence, explicitly tell students to copy/record it before advancing; later slides normally use student notes rather than re-displaying prior evidence
do not add compact carry-forward evidence boxes unless explicitly teacher-requested or genuinely required for accessibility/safety
final slide contains 2-4 discussion questions plus bridge into instruction
functional cut/sort cards may use borders
task content uses open hierarchy rather than nested boxes
workspace only where students need to record thinking

teacher_guide.rule: same shared teacher-guide surface for Demo and Investigation guides; preserve practical overview first
teacher_guide.demo_after_overview: one detail page per slide with slide replica occupying the top half and detailed notes below (expected responses, what to notice, teacher moves, misconceptions/transition as relevant)
teacher_guide.investigation_after_overview: answered student walkthrough: recognizable replicas of substantive student tasks followed by answers/solutions and rationale/what-to-listen-for; keep Strong Synthesis in the overview AND finish with a student-style synthesis replica plus acceptable responses/rationale/teacher presses
teacher_guide.table_style: clean compact tables with clear navy/soft-blue headers, restrained row separation, and centered numerical data where appropriate

caption_rule: Student-facing graphs/tables/diagrams/images have no descriptive captions beneath them. Necessary mathematical labels stay inside the representation.
legacy_css_guard: The accidentally named investigations.css/activity_stations.css is NOT a Demos/Investigations stylesheet and must never be selected for Investigation student HTML.
